setupSteps: Floor and mat: use a non-slip mat or carpet on a firm floor. A soft bed lets the body sink and hides your range.
Noise: the movement is quiet. Place the mat so your feet are not touching a wall and your hands have room ahead of you.
Lie face down: a folded towel under the hips or forehead is allowed if the pelvis or kneecaps press uncomfortably (Hinge Health and others suggest padding if needed).
Legs: straight, about hip-width apart (Healthline), toes pointing back, feet relaxed. Squeeze the buttocks lightly before you lift.

Arms: stretch them straight ahead along the floor, shoulder-width apart, palms down (the usual start). Easier alternative: arms by your sides or in a "goalpost" position with elbows bent (physiotherapy sources use hands by the side or behind the back for easier loading, est.).

Head and neck: forehead resting on the floor, or a gaze on a spot just ahead of your hands. The neck stays long and in line with the spine (sources advise a slightly tucked chin and eyes down, not looking ahead).
Brace: gently draw the belly button up towards the spine, as if tightening a belt a notch (sources suggest this light brace). Do not hold your breath.
Clothing: fitted top and leggings or track pants so the camera can see shoulders, hips, knees and ankles. Loose kurtas hide the hip line.
Water: keep a bottle nearby; this is light work, but long holds feel long.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Lie down and set the start
steps.action: Lie face down, arms stretched ahead, legs straight and hip-width apart, forehead on the floor.
steps.feel: Whole front of the body resting; calm back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: shoulders, hips, knees and ankles in one low line on the mat. Front: arms level and shoulder-width apart.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Brace gently
steps.action: Lightly draw the belly button up from the floor and squeeze the buttocks.
steps.feel: Slight tightness low in the belly and buttocks.
steps.visualCheck: Side: nothing has lifted yet; neck still in line.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Lift the limbs a hand's width
steps.action: Raise both arms and both legs only a few centimetres, 5-8 cm (est.; sources say a few inches), keeping the head in line with the spine.
steps.feel: Work along the lower and mid back and buttocks. No pinch in the lower back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: only the limbs rise; the chest barely lifts and the neck stays long. Front: arms and legs rise evenly.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Pause
steps.action: Hold the lift without lifting higher.
steps.feel: Steady work in the back and glutes.
steps.visualCheck: Knees straight, elbows straight, head not rising.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Lower slowly
steps.action: Lower arms and legs back to the mat under control.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Rest between reps
steps.action: Rest your cheek or forehead on the floor for a breath.

steps.part: A. Lower-range beginner superman (arms and legs together, small lift)
steps.title: Finish the set
steps.action: After the last rep rest, then push back into Child's Pose (Yoga & Stretch 8) if comfortable.
steps.visualCheck: Stop the set early if the neck strained or the lower back pinched.

steps.part: B. Alternating "bird-dog style" prone lift (right arm with left leg, then switch)
steps.title: Lie face down, arms stretched ahead, legs hip-width apart, forehead on the floor; brace as above

steps.part: B. Alternating "bird-dog style" prone lift (right arm with left leg, then switch)
steps.title: Breathe out and lift the right arm and the left leg together, a few centimetres only, while the left arm and right leg stay down (this is the same diagonal pairing as the all-fours bird dog; the Healthline bird-dog guide describes extending one arm and the opposite leg)

steps.part: B. Alternating "bird-dog style" prone lift (right arm with left leg, then switch)
steps.title: Pause 1-2 seconds, lower slowly (about 2 seconds), then switch sides

steps.part: B. Alternating "bird-dog style" prone lift (right arm with left leg, then switch)
steps.title: Keep the hips level on the mat; do not let the body roll or twist. This is a prone lift, so it is not exactly a bird dog; the all-fours bird dog (hands and knees) is a separate exercise and is listed in the swaps

steps.part: B. Alternating "bird-dog style" prone lift (right arm with left leg, then switch)
steps.title: For the hold option, stay up 3-5 seconds per side at first (the bird dog is commonly taught with holds of a few seconds to 10 seconds; Harvard Health's "Three moves for better spine health" shows a 10-second bird-dog hold, which is a different exercise)
Lift both arms, both legs and the chest together to a low-to-moderate height, with the head in line
Hold 2-3 seconds for reps, or 5-10 seconds for the hold option. Keep breathing
Lower slowly. Stop the set if the lower back pinches or the neck tightens

commonMistakes.title: Lifting the head too high or looking forward
commonMistakes.text: Lifting the head too high or looking forward. Why: strains the neck; it is the most cited error. Fix: forehead near the floor, eyes down, chin slightly tucked.

commonMistakes.title: Lifting arms and legs too high (hard low-back arch)
commonMistakes.text: Lifting arms and legs too high (hard low-back arch). Why: a hard arch pinches the lower back and does not add useful work. Fix: lift only a hand's width and stop if you feel a pinch.

commonMistakes.title: Kicking up with momentum
commonMistakes.text: Kicking up with momentum. Why: fast reps lose muscle control and raise injury risk. Fix: 2 s up, 2-3 s pause, 2 s down (est.).

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: breath-holding raises blood pressure more than open breathing during effort (lab data from heavy lifting, PubMed 7741618). Fix: steady breaths; breathe out while lifting.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears. Why: the neck and upper traps take over. Fix: slide the shoulder blades down and back before the lift.

commonMistakes.title: Bent knees or flopping legs
commonMistakes.text: Bent knees or flopping legs. Why: the glutes and hamstrings are not working through a straight line. Fix: straight legs, toes pointing back.

commonMistakes.title: Twisting or rolling the hips in the alternating version
commonMistakes.text: Twisting or rolling the hips in the alternating version. Why: the lower back twists instead of resisting. Fix: smaller lift, keep both hips pressed to the mat.

commonMistakes.title: Doing it with pain
commonMistakes.text: Doing it with pain. Why: sources say people with chronic low back pain or recent back injury may not be suited to it (Healthline). Fix: stop, rest, and use a gentler alternative (swaps below) or see a clinician.

safetyNotes: Back problems: Healthline says it may not suit chronic lower back pain or a recent back injury; a physiotherapy guide says prone extension can aggravate extension-intolerant backs. Use the lower-range version in a pain-free range; stop if pain increases, spreads down a leg, or you feel numbness.
Neck or shoulder problems: keep the head resting and limit arm height; use arms by the sides.
High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe steadily, avoid breath-holding, get up slowly from the floor; get clearance for severe or uncontrolled BP or known heart disease.
Pregnancy and postpartum: lying on the stomach is uncomfortable in later pregnancy (an inference); a doctor's advice is needed. After childbirth, ask a physiotherapist, especially after a C-section.
Recent surgery (especially back or abdominal), dizziness or balance problems on the floor: only with approval.
Osteoporosis: back-extensor strengthening is recommended in research, but forceful, high-range arching is not; individual advice is needed.

conditionCautions.change: Light effort (3-4/10, Borg 9-11); short holds of 2-5 s; breathe out on effort and never hold the breath; rise slowly; severe or uncontrolled BP needs a medical check first
Counts as resistance work; usual glucose checks and fast carbohydrate on hand if on insulin or sulfonylureas; check feet if neuropathy
After clearance only: lower-range lift at light effort, steady breathing, short holds; stop with chest discomfort or breathlessness
conditionCautions.source: AHA physical activity recommendations; clearance specifics Not found
